text:
Maria Chen: quick design idea — adaptive slab granularity + lease protocol for tensorpool. want to reduce OOM noise and improve reuse for activations/logits/scratchpads.

Kevin Patel: curious, what do you mean by "adaptive" here? dynamic slab sizes?

Maria Chen: yeah. runtime picks slab grain based on three signals: recent max alloc, KV cache hit pressure, and kernel selection (fused vs unfused). smaller grain for high-fragmentation jobs, larger grain for stable long-lived KV-heavy requests.

Ashwin Rao: sounds promising. do you have perf numbers or a simple sim?

Maria Chen: quick sim from yesterday — microbench harness (single GPU, seq_len=2048, batch=8): baseline pool: avg latency 34.2ms, p95 78ms, OOMs seen in 4/200 runs. adaptive-gran = avg 33.7ms, p95 66ms, OOMs 0/200. Not production yet but consistent in harness.

Devon Liu: impressive on OOMs. where does lease protocol fit?

Maria Chen: lease = short-term exclusive lease for scratchpads/logits during kernel execution + soft reclaim after kernel completes if not pinned. leases decay fast for short kernels (flash attention) and longer for KV-heavy calls. prevents long-lived allocations blocking reuse.

Kevin Patel: how does this interact with batching heuristics? e.g., if batcher suddenly combines many requests and kernel selects fused op, could lease durations confuse reuse and cause latency spikes?

Maria Chen: good point. lease TTL is jittered and tied to batching path decision. we record kernel hints at enqueue time: batcher labels group with kernel_hint (fused|unfused|split). allocator consults group hint to decide whether to extend lease slightly.

Ashwin Rao: we need to be careful with correctness around parallel kernels. maybe add an assert mode to detect double-free races.

Maria Chen: already on it — bench-bot integrates small assert mode. run example:

```
./bench-harness --profile --seq 2048 --batch 8 --mode assert-lease
```

bench-bot: ran 50 iterations in assert mode, 0 double-free, 0 race detected, avg 34.0ms baseline vs 33.6ms adaptive. logs uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/2468/lease-assert.log

Devon Liu: any kernel-selector regressions? last time we tuned kernels we saw a p99 regression on short sequences.

Maria Chen: yes we ran into a regression on seq<=32 after changing eager-free ordering in allocator; root cause was eviction policy thrashing with very small slabs. adaptive grain plus lease reduces scavenging frequency for tiny seqs.

Kevin Patel: can you paste the profiling flame for a regressed run? just the hotspots and mem ops.

Maria Chen: pasted snippet:

```
HOTSPOTS:
  - compute_kernels 54% (flash_attn fused)
  - alloc/scavenge 18% (freelist walk)
  - kv-cache copy 12% (pin/unpin)
  - kernel_launch_latency 8%
```

Maria Chen: observed that freelist walk cost correlated with slab grain mismatch. smaller grains -> more freelist entries -> higher overhead in tight loops. adaptive aims to reduce freelist traversal cost by coalescing when beneficial.

Ashwin Rao: implementation detail question: do you want slab coalescing to be lock-free or protected by a thin spin? collisions could degrade.

Maria Chen: prefer per-thread local freelists + cooperative coalesce under epoch fence. coarse locks only for rare global ops. keeps the fast path lock-free.

Devon Liu: how about telemetry? we need counters: lease_acquired, lease_reclaimed, lease_staled, slab_coalesces, freelist_walks. also sample per model id and kernel_hint.

Maria Chen: agreed. adding these to runtime metrics and to per-request baggage. propose we run a staged canary on Dedicated with 5% traffic next week.

Kevin Patel: rollout plan sounds fine. add kill-switch config: allocator.mode = "adaptive-lease:off|on|canary" and an overseer detector to revert auto.

Maria Chen: will draft PR with config and sim results. cc @Ashwin for review on lock design.

Ashwin Rao: happy to review. one more ask: include a small reproducer that triggers the seq<=32 regression so SRE can validate revert path quickly.

Maria Chen: will include reproducer and a short runbook for SRE. thanks all. :tada:

Devon Liu: love it — small nit: add test for mixed KV + non-KV workloads; those hit weird paths.

Maria Chen: yep adding mixed workload tests. will post PR link when ready.

bench-bot: deploy check — CI preflight passed, rustfmt ok, unit tests 412/412.
